mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an easing monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points indicates labor market deterioration that precedes corporate earnings contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.2pp over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signals robust consumer demand that drives corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS rise by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: In a recessionary regime, a monthly industrial production decline exceeding 0.3 percentage points indicates economic contraction that reduces corporate profitability, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls by more than 0.3% and the regime is recessionary.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly federal funds rate increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals aggressive monetary tightening that raises corporate borrowing costs, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5pp over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate decline below 4.0% indicates a tight labor market that supports wage growth and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous quarterly GDP growth and rising inflation signal strong economic expansion with pricing power, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 grows by at least 1.0% quarter-over-quarter and CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals manufacturing sector strength that boosts corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO increases by more than 0.5% over the prior month.
